info.title: inhuman-harness daemon RPC
info.description: HTTP projection of the daemon contract, generated from @inhuman.tools/harness-contract. The daemon's only transport today is JSON-RPC 2.0 over WebSocket (see openrpc.json); each operation here names its wire method in `x-rpc-method`.

post.summary: Write a key in session, project or kernel scope
post.description: Session `model` / `connection` also become the last-choice default (project + kernel) when `remember` is set. `/model` and `/connect` send "1"; a bare session write (subagent, `--model`, `--connection`) does not.

post.summary: Clear a key in session, project or kernel scope
Call a plugin's own state method
post.description: A plugin command's call into that plugin's own state. `args` is a JSON object, since action params cross as strings. `field` names the argument the composer text (`input`) fills; an empty `input` then refuses. A failure is data (`ok: false`), not an RPC error.

post.summary: Set the session's permission mode
Explain what would happen to a call right now
post.description: Runs the same floor, grant and resolution code as a real call, with no judge and no effect. Returns the tier (block, soft-deny, ask, allow), the classes that voted, which resolver licenses it in the session's mode and from which layer, and the outcome.

post.summary: Set or clear this session's authorization overlay
post.description: A human decision for this session only. It may loosen what the user's config says, but never past the project layer. Refused for any caller that is not a human client.

post.summary: Read the authorization layers this session resolves against
Adopt a connection and make it this session's connection
post.description: Delegates to the kernel's `connect/adopt`, then writes the new connection id into the session's `connection` key and warms it. May park for UI.

post.summary: Submit a prompt as a turn, a steer or a queued prompt
post.description: Pictures (`visuals`) ride only on a fresh turn: standard base64, stored beside the session, and the model must accept images.

post.summary: Cancel a running turn by turn id or eval request id
Read one picture seated on the session's head turn
Rewind the session to before a turn
Retry the last turn
Read one blob the session's document references, by content hash
post.description: Large bodies (a file's prior text today) live in the kernel's blob bucket; the document keeps `{sha256, bytes, mime, head}`. `text/*` blobs return `text`, anything else `bytesBase64`. The hash a document names is the capability; there is no listing.

post.summary: Move the session's large stored text into the blob bucket
post.description: A session written before large bodies left the document keeps a file's prior text and an isolated completion's prompt inline, and the stored image carries them forever. The vacuum moves every such body over the inline limit into the kernel's blob bucket, leaving the head and a reference, then rewrites the stored image as one snapshot. Completions still running are skipped. `dryRun` counts what would move and writes nothing. Reads stay whole: the wire projection and `blob/get` resolve the references.

post.summary: Compact the session's context, optionally around a focus
Set the session title
Admit a Scheme program as an unattended eval turn
post.description: Idempotent per `requestId`: a repeat with the same input returns the admitted turn; a repeat with different input is refused. `ok: false` with `policy_unavailable` means the requested permission policy cannot run unattended.

post.summary: Answer the live approval ask
post.description: Answer the live ask or soft-deny on `sessionId`: this session, or a worker that escalated to it. `store` remembers a human yes to an ask as a grant (scope, subject, TTL); a soft-deny is never stored and a block is never put to a human.

post.summary: List calls waiting for an acknowledgement
post.description: A call that is allowed but flagged `needsAcknowledgement` waits for a person. Acks travel over RPC only: there is no ack job and no transcript entry. Absent `sessionId`: this session and the workers that escalated to it.

post.summary: Acknowledge or refuse a pending call, optionally remembering the acknowledgement
post.description: Human clients only. `accept` lets the call run; a refusal is a human denial (its `comment` is what the agent reads). `store` remembers the acknowledgement at session, project, bot or global scope as one of the offered `storeOptions`; prompt-created project, bot and global acks last 7 days. A block and a policy denial are never put here. When the prompt was also an ask (a combined prompt), the same answer settles both.

post.summary: Mark the session resident (kept alive) or not
Promote the first queued prompt to a steer
post.description: A queued row named by the id the client saw. Already drained or moved is `ok: false`.

post.summary: Retract the last queued prompt
post.description: A queued row named by the id the client saw. Already drained or moved is `ok: false`.

post.summary: List agent calls made from this session
Inspect one agent call by request id
Cancel one agent call by request id
Remember which session a terminal key continues
Forget a terminal key's continue session
Remove a connection and its secrets
post.description: Without `confirm: true` it parks on a confirmation form; cancelling answers `{ok: false}`.

post.summary: Adopt a connection from a driver
post.description: Runs the driver's adopt flow. The flow may need the human (sign-in, a pasted key) and then parks. Cancelling answers `{ok: false}`.

post.summary: List connections, optionally by ability claim
Probe the model catalog of one or all connections
Read one connection with its settings
Enable or disable a connection
Always allow one tool of a connection
Exclude one tool of a connection
Sign in to a connection
post.description: May open a browser flow and park until the human finishes it.

post.summary: Sign out of a connection
Rename a connection or merge its settings
post.description: Rename or merge settings of a connection that already exists. The id stays.

post.summary: Adopt an MCP server as a connection
post.description: May need the human (sign-in) and then parks.

post.summary: Search the official MCP registry
Set kernel configuration fields
List stored grants
Store a grant from settings
post.description: A grant turns an ask into allow for a family (a command, a path, an MCP server+tool+account). It never lifts a soft-deny or a block. Settings grants do not expire unless `ttlMs` is given.

post.summary: Revoke a stored grant
List stored acknowledgements
post.description: The acknowledgements a person stored at session, project, bot or global scope (same rows, TTL and scopes as grants). Flags themselves live in the `authorization` block (see `policy/config-get`).

post.summary: Store an acknowledgement from settings
post.description: Equivalent to "you can send any email you want in this project". Settings acknowledgements do not expire unless `ttlMs` is given.

post.summary: Revoke a stored acknowledgement
Enable, disable or foreground a plugin
Install a plugin from an npm spec
Remove an installed plugin
List skill files for a project and home
Write a skill file
Remove a skill file
Read a skill file with its body
Sign in for remote access
post.description: WorkOS device login. Parks on an open-url form until the human approves in the browser; cancelling answers `{ok: false}`. Fails when `HARNESS_REMOTE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` is unset.

post.summary: Remote access state of this machine
Drop remote access tokens
post.description: Keeps the machine id, so signing in again reuses the same machine.

post.summary: Write a bot definition
post.description: Absent `invokes`, `reasoningEffort` and `modelPreferences` keep the file's current value; an empty list clears. Absent `mcp` keeps the file's grants; an empty list clears them. A settings save that does not know these fields must not wipe them.

post.summary: Remove a bot definition
Answer a parked UI form
post.description: Finishes a call that answered `{form: "ui", pending, body}`. The reply is the resumed call's result, or another park form. `kind: "cancel"` aborts the parked call. Closing the socket cancels every park it owns.
